title: Financial Services Compensation Scheme of Last Resort Levy (Collection) Bill 2023
short_title: Financial Services Compensation Scheme of Last Resort Levy (Collection) Bill 2023

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish collection and administration rules for industry levies funding the financial services compensation scheme of last resort and related unpaid complaints fees.
The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) would gather information, issue payment notices and collect levy debts and penalties on behalf of the Commonwealth.
It would operate alongside the separate levy imposition bill, with collection legislation commencing only if that companion legislation commences, under the joint compensation scheme package.
changes: Annual levy payment notices would allow at least 30 days before the payment date.
A false or misleading statement causing underpayment could trigger a penalty twice the shortfall, unless reasonable care steps were taken.
ASIC could waive levies or penalties in exceptional circumstances.
Failures to provide required information or substantiation could attract strict liability offences, subject to reasonable excuse protections.
summary.affected: Liable financial services businesses, ASIC and the compensation scheme operator are affected.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Bills on financial accountability, financial services compensation, health, national security, education and vocational training were referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration. The speaker also remarked that they hoped their next speech would be more interesting.

speeches.speaker: Angus Taylor
speeches.brief: The government’s mismanagement of the Financial Accountability Regime bills, including a deal with the Greens that was later reversed, delayed their passage, and it broke promises on tax and superannuation, such as doubling super taxes and taxing unrealised capital gains, while the Levy review on financial advice remains unanswered.
